title: Today in one sentence
text: Stocks closed Tuesday with Meta up 2.6% and AMD up 1.9%, while Rocket Lab fell 2.3%; the thing to watch tomorrow is the inflation report at 8:30 am Eastern, and then TSMC's report card on Thursday morning.

title: Inflation report is tomorrow
text: The September inflation report (how fast prices are rising) comes out Wednesday, Oct. 14. One analyst preview expects prices to be up about 3.6% from a year ago, compared with 3.4% in August. That is only a forecast. If the real number is higher, the Fed may keep interest rates high, and stocks that cost a lot compared with their profits, like AMD, often feel it most. The Fed meets again Oct. 27 to 28.

title: TSMC reports on Thursday
text: TSMC makes chips for NVIDIA, AMD and Broadcom, so its report card is a clue for the whole AI chip business. It reports Thursday, Oct. 15, at 2:00 am Eastern. TSMC closed Tuesday at $445.12, about 9% below its highest price of the past year ($487.47). Its own forecast for the quarter was sales of $44.6 to $45.8 billion; the real numbers could be better or worse.

title: Meta led the day
text: Meta rose 2.6% to $762.50, close to its one-year high of $779.82. Reports say the move followed Meta's launch of new AI models and several analyst price target increases. Experts' average price target is $800.30, only 5% above where the stock closed. When a stock has already run up, there is less room left to reach what experts guess.

title: Health and industrial stocks slipped
text: Among Nasdaq companies, healthcare fell 1.7% and industrials fell 1.8% on average, while energy and utilities rose about 1.8%. In our list, Eli Lilly fell 1.4%, Intuitive Surgical fell 1.3% and Lockheed Martin fell 1.5%. One day of moves is a small piece of the story, not a trend.

title: Lesson 5: What is a P/E ratio?
text: P/E means price divided by earnings. Earnings are a company's profit for each share over the last year. If a stock costs $100 and the company earned $5 per share, the P/E is 20. You are paying $20 for every $1 of yearly profit. Today Alphabet's P/E is about 17, Microsoft's is about 30, and AMD's is about 154. A high P/E often means people expect fast growth, and a stock with a high P/E can fall harder if the growth is disappointing. A low P/E is not always a bargain either; sometimes the company is growing slowly. P/E works best when you compare similar companies.

title: What we could and could not check
text: Prices, 52-week ranges and expert price targets come from FMP, and prices are Tuesday's close. Experts' targets and company numbers were not available for Broadcom, Vertiv, Rocket Lab, Eli Lilly and Intuitive Surgical, so those spots are empty. The inflation forecast comes from one analyst preview, not from the government. Company and news websites could not be opened today, so the TSMC date and forecast were confirmed through search results that point to TSMC's own page, and the Meta reason comes from a search summary and is not fully confirmed. This is information to learn from, not advice to buy or sell.
